candidates.title: §4.6's pre-existing "taken over ... silently" claim now overlaps confusingly with the newly-written lock_taken paragraph
candidates.detail: Line 311 (untouched by this diff) says a generated holder "is taken over on the next call by anyone, silently." Five lines later, the diff's new paragraph (lines 316-320) draws a much narrower silence: only a generated *acquirer* taking over a generated holder, unforced, "records nothing" — a named acquirer's takeover of the same generated holder does append a lock_taken event (cmd_next.go's `case orphaned:` when `!r.genID`, internal/cli/cmd_next.go:206-209). Reusing the word "silently" for the (unrelated, still-true) absence of the `ask: owner` prompt right next to a paragraph that uses "quietly"/"records nothing" for the absence of an audit event invites a reader to conflate the two. Task 3's brief only asked for the one sentence at ~line 315 to be rewritten, but the result now reads as self-contradictory within the same subsection unless line 311 is also qualified.

candidates.title: Rewritten §4.6 sentence omits the generated-acquirer/named-holder case
candidates.detail: The new sentence enumerates recording as 'when a named session takes over' or 'whenever a takeover was explicitly forced', plus the generated-over-generated exemption and the no-takeover case. It does not mention the (unchanged, pre-existing) case where a *generated* acquirer takes over a *stale named* holder without --force: since `orphaned` is false there (the holder isn't `Generated`), the code's default arm in internal/cli/cmd_next.go still appends lock_taken (outcome LockStolen) regardless of the acquirer's own kind or the force flag. A reader could infer from 'recorded when a named session takes over' that a generated acquirer's takeover of a stale named holder goes unrecorded, which is not true. The code is correct and unchanged in this respect; only the doc's new three-part framing leaves this combination unstated.

candidates.title: New default: arm of the lock_taken switch has no test asserting its event shape
candidates.detail: Task-3 rewrote the last switch arm from an explicit outcome check (`case outcome == bundle.LockStolen, outcome == bundle.LockForced && r.force:`) to a bare `default:` (cmd_next.go:207-210), which only the not-orphaned path reaches (a named/non-generated holder being stolen or forced). The new `case !takeover:` guard that makes this safe is well covered by TestNextForceWithoutATakeoverAppendsNothing (cmd_next_test.go:1512), and the exemption change is covered by TestNextExplicitForceOverAGeneratedHolderAppendsLockTaken (cmd_next_test.go:1462) — but that test only exercises generated holders, which are always `orphaned` regardless of heartbeat freshness (orphaned only checks held.Generated + ID mismatch, not staleness), so both its idle and live scenarios land in `case orphaned:`, not `default:`. The only code path that actually reaches `default:` is a named-holder takeover, exercised behaviorally by the pre-existing TestNextSessionLock (cmd_next_test.go:881-899), but that test never inspects the appended lock_taken event's fields (outcome value, absence of a `reason` key). No test in the diff (or found in the file) asserts `eventsOfType(...)[0].Data` for a forced/stolen takeover of a non-generated holder, so a regression in this specific arm (e.g., an accidental `reason` key, or a wrong outcome value) would not be caught.

candidates.title: Fault-injection test helpers duplicated verbatim across two test files
candidates.detail: readOnlyEventLog/directoryEventLog (internal/cli/cmd_record_test.go:338-368) and breakEventAppend/breakEventRead (internal/cli/record_reviewer_test.go:549-579) are byte-for-byte identical implementations (same os.Chmod(0o400)/OpenFile probe/os.Remove+os.Mkdir dance), differing only in name. They live in different Go packages (cli vs cli_test) so they can't call each other directly, but internal/testutil (a package already imported by both, e.g. testutil.NewRepo/testutil.Git) is the natural home for a single testutil.BreakEventAppend(t, bdir)/testutil.BreakEventRead(t, bdir) pair — confirmed via grep that os.Chmod(p, 0o400) and Mkdir(p, 0o750) each appear in exactly these two new locations and nowhere pre-existing in the tree. Not blocking, but ~30 duplicated lines that a shared helper would remove.

candidates.title: warnStreakLoss inlines its warning string instead of following the local excludeWarning(err) helper convention
candidates.detail: cmd_init.go's excludeWarning(err) (internal/cli/cmd_init.go:425-427) is a small named function returning "info/exclude not written: " + err.Error(), used by both cmd_init.go and cmd_next.go for the same warnings-contract pattern this task extends. warnStreakLoss instead builds "attempt-streak reset not recorded: "+err.Error() inline inside the append call. Not wrong, but it departs from the one-sentence-per-named-function shape the warnings contract otherwise uses for its two other producers.

verdicts.evidence: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-24-takt-design.md:311 says a generated holder 'is taken over on the next call by anyone, silently' — this describes the absence of the `ask: owner` prompt (the next sentences, lines 314-315, introduce that gate: 'If another id holds the lock with a heartbeat younger than lock_ttl... next returns ask: owner'). The new paragraph at lines 316-319 uses 'quietly' (not 'silently') for a distinct, clearly-scoped concept — whether the lock_taken audit event is appended — and explicitly explains the event contract ('The lock_taken event records a takeover, not a flag'). Both spans are individually true and describe different mechanisms (prompt-gating vs. audit-logging); there is no actual contradiction, only a speculative claim that a reader 'could' conflate two different words ('silently' vs 'quietly') used for two clearly delineated topics five lines apart. No factual error is shown.

The rewritten sentence enumerates recording conditions as 'a **named** session takes over' or 'a takeover was **explicitly forced**', plus the generated-over-generated and nothing-taken exemptions — but omits the case of a generated acquirer stealing a stale *named* (non-generated) holder without --force. Code confirms this case is recorded unconditionally: bundle.Acquire (internal/bundle/lock.go:38-39) returns LockStolen purely from `now.Sub(held.Heartbeat) > ttl`, with no dependence on who or force; back in cmd_next.go, `orphaned := held != nil && held.ID != r.session && held.Generated` (cmd_next.go:130) is false for a named holder, so the switch's `orphaned && r.genID && !r.force` and `case orphaned:` arms are skipped and it falls to `default:` (cmd_next.go:210-213), which appends lock_taken regardless of the acquirer's own kind. The doc's enumerated 'yes' list (named acquirer / explicit force) does not literally state this generated-acquirer-over-named-holder case.

The `default:` arm (cmd_next.go:210-213) is reached only by non-orphaned takeovers. TestNextExplicitForceOverAGeneratedHolderAppendsLockTaken (cmd_next_test.go:1462-1502) uses only Generated:true holders, both idle and live, which are always `orphaned` per `orphaned := held != nil && held.ID != r.session && held.Generated` (cmd_next.go:130) — so both scenarios hit `case orphaned:`, never `default:`. The only test that reaches `default:` is TestNextSessionLock (cmd_next_test.go:892-894), `if _, o, _ := next(t, root, b, "--force"); o["op"] != "run"` — this checks only the op, never `eventsOfType(t, bdir, "lock_taken")[0].Data`. A grep across the package confirms no test asserts `Data["outcome"]` or absence of a reason key for this arm.

readOnlyEventLog/directoryEventLog (cmd_record_test.go:340-368) and breakEventAppend/breakEventRead (record_reviewer_test.go:627-654) are line-for-line identical (same os.Chmod(p, 0o400)/OpenFile probe/Cleanup, same os.Remove+os.Mkdir(p, 0o750) dance), differing only in name. Confirmed the files are in different packages: cmd_record_test.go:2 is `package cli`, record_reviewer_test.go:1 is `package cli_test`. Both already import internal/testutil (cmd_record_test.go:288 `testutil.NewRepo(t)`; record_reviewer_test.go:14 import, used at line 26+). A grep for os.Chmod(p, 0o400) and Mkdir(p, 0o750) finds them only at these two new locations in the source tree.

cmd_init.go defines `func excludeWarning(err error) string { return "info/exclude not written: " + err.Error() }` (cmd_init.go:425-427), used by both cmd_init.go and cmd_next.go (cmd_next.go:160 `r.warnings = append(r.warnings, excludeWarning(err))`) — a small named function per warning sentence. warnStreakLoss instead builds the string inline: `out[keyWarnings] = append(prev, "attempt-streak reset not recorded: "+err.Error())` (facts.go:281), with no equivalent named helper. This is an accurate, quotable description of the stylistic departure.
